summary: Bailey-chain / q-series generators need a q-parameter and a chain recursion; the repo's growing-level identity programme (GROWING_IDENTITIES.md, exact identities with level growing with n) and the k-indexed power ladder (POWER_LADDER_ES.md) already are the 'identities indexed by a growing parameter' idea. No Bailey pair was constructed.

Local solubility with denominators sharing primes with n is the Bright–Loughran setting (arXiv:1908.02526, Br U_n/Br Q = Z/2, no BM obstruction), already recorded in B2_ACROSS_FIELDS.md; the literal mod-N statement is vacuous (x=y=z=0 solves it), so the nontrivial reading is BL's.

Fermat-number and 3·2^s+1 families are settled (BRAINSTORM/z15_proth_sophie_germain.md: ES for all 3·2^s+1 proved as an ET-sterile family); 4·3^k+1 and other a·b^k+c families are the power-ladder programme in POWER_LADDER_ES.md.

The Hardy-field generalisation is in POINTWISE_SIZE.md (threshold results hold for Hardy fields) and the exp-log identity test is the ES_(k) ladder in POWER_LADDER_ES.md, where odd squares lose all certificate lines (T1 dies for the rung).

Computed e-slice failure densities for e = 3,7,11,15,19 over 8977 primes p ≡ 1 (4), p < 2·10⁵ (success iff e/M = 1/y+1/z solvable, M = p(p+e)/4). Unconditioned joint ratios P(both fail)/(P·P) reach 2.3 (e=3,19), but conditioning on p mod 24 collapses them to 0.4–1.6 (ratios near 1 in most cells), so the correlation is a class effect.

Computed D(p) = #{M ≤ 1000: p is a square mod M} for 1611 primes p ≡ 1 (4), p ≤ 3·10⁴: Spearman with U = −0.37. Adding D to a character model (prime q < 80) raises R² by 0.126, but D is mostly the class-of-one and 2-adic structure: after adding 2-adic indicators and 1[p ≡ 1 mod m] for m ≤ 32 the gain is 0.004. Already covered by H00 Z0199 and the 2-adic entries of the fingerprint lane.

Literature: Ford (arXiv:math/0401223; Ann. Math. 168, 2008) gives the order of H(x,y,z) = #{n ≤ x: n has a divisor in (y,z]}; Bloom–Elsholtz (TU Graz survey) describes the ET divisor-in-interval argument. The snippets show no Ford-type lower-tail exponent entering the ET Type I/II bounds, and the item names no quantity to measure, so nothing was tested.
Type I-only / Type II-only fits with dividing-avoid samples were done in the z52b dividing lane (BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md, scripts/z52b_dividing_avoid.py, data/z52b/dividing_avoid_X3000.txt).

Reproduced from f4_all_30000.txt: U(n) = 5 occurs 0 times for 2 ≤ n ≤ 30000 (values 1,2,3,4,6,7,8 occur; the largest n with U(n) ≤ 8 is 241). Already fingerprint-0007 in BRAINSTORM/z52b_fingerprint.md. Extension to 10⁵ not run.

Searching primes ≡ 1 (mod 360360) up to 10¹⁰ for extreme L(1, χ_p) and counting U on the top candidates needs about 6.6·10³ primes ≤ 10¹⁰ and a U-count per prime of order p/2 x-values with divisor enumeration, i.e. several CPU-hours (>1 h). Not run.
next: Rank the ~6.6·10³ primes ≡ 1 (mod 360360) up to 10¹⁰ by L(1,χ_p) (cheap), count U on the top 10³ with a sped-up counter, compare U/log³p with 276.

Mean (★) Cmin by p mod 840 over primes ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 1.2·10⁷: the top class is 37 (mean 8.3, driven by the single record 23105 at p = 184837) and the square class 361 has the highest mean among the six Mordell classes (4.13; 1: 2.88, 169: 3.02, 289: 2.83, 121: 2.67, 529: 2.53). The mean is record-dominated, so the square classes are not the Cmin-hardest; a median was not computed.

No repo memo covers Carmichael numbers in the ES count. The compounding test (semiprimes pq with both p, q hard) was not run; the sample is too small to add a claim.

Cmin records (1,2,5,...,557, then 23105 at p = 184837) are already in BRAINSTORM/z52b_fingerprint.md item 180. The boundary-only classification needs the minwords file, which is absent from the data tree, so not rerun.

Interior (★) words (u, v ≥ 2) over primes ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 1.2·10⁷: 14 primes have no (★) word at all (the R-zeros), and 45 more have only boundary words (cm > 0 but cmi = 0), e.g. 5, 13, 17, 29, 37, 53, 97. This gives a second, larger list of boundary-only primes; no further structure was tested.
I3 record sizes and the I3 word data are in the fingerprint lane (BRAINSTORM/z52b_fingerprint.md) and I3_DEEP_FABLE.md; the growth fit against p needs the words file (absent), so not refit here.

Computed the first witness level Cform(p) (min C with a divisor a ≡ −1 mod 4C of 4Cp+1) for 1125 primes ≡ 1 (4), p < 2·10⁴, C ≤ 50. The product of marginals overpredicts the joint: P(Cform>c)/∏q_C ≈ 0.5–0.7 for c ≥ 3, but this is the p ≡ 2 (mod 3) effect: 3 | 4p+1 gives a = 3 ≡ −1 mod 4 as a level-1 witness (already noted in ES_CONNECTIONS_TODO Z0351). Within mod-24 classes the ratios are noisy (0.5–0.9).
The coprime-pair failure list (primes 13, 37, 61, 97, ...) is in data/z52b/variants.json and variants2.json (variants lane); the mod-12 claim and failure density were not rechecked.

Partial only: variants.json stores 40 of the 110 primitive-failure primes (head 30 and tail 10), and none of them is one of the six R-zero primes ≤ 98713 (409, 577, 5569, 9601, 23929, 83449). The full hypergeometric test needs the complete primitive-failure set for primes ≤ 10⁵, i.e. full solution enumeration for the 110 failing primes up to x ≤ 3p/4 (about 10⁷ factorisations, >1 h).
next: Enumerate all primitive solutions for the 110 failing primes ≤ 10⁵ (solver), intersect with the R-zero set, and report the hypergeometric p-value.

summary: The BM residual correlation with U at 20 000–30 000 (+0.58) is already in data/z52b/bm_check_20000_30000.json; the recomputed BM main term for ESC was not rerun.

Reproduced the easiest classes mod 840 from f4_all_30000 (top five by mean U/log²p: 557, 277, 653, 797, 317; batch1). The per-class identity-family multiplicity count was not run (see MODEL_SPECIFIC.md).

The enrichment is usable but rests on 14 events.

Tested against A396825 (b-file to n = 16384): all R&U zeros ≡ 1 (4) up to 1369 lie in A396825 except 105; the R-zeros ≡ 1 (4) up to 1369 are not contained in A396825 (12 of 31 lie outside: 57, 105, 177, 249, 345, 409, 465, 577, 777, 801, 969, 1345).

A400619 record prime 8803369 (p mod 840 = 169): minimal (★) C = 4 and minimal U-word v = 12, so it is not a (★) zero; 8813281 (≡ 1 mod 840) is an R-zero (no (★) word at all) with minimal v = 8. Minima only, no word counts R(p) were computed.

Among n ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 16384 the joint (★)&U zeros are exactly the 65 odd squares plus 105, all contained in A396825 ∪ {105, 672}. So containment holds to 16384 but only because the zero set is the squares plus 105; the earlier 1380 hit was n ≡ 0 (mod 4) and is outside the ESC class.
Per-class identity signatures mod 840 are the subject of MODEL_SPECIFIC.md; the ratio-bucket census per class is in data/z52b/spectral.json.

Ratio buckets of the smallest denominator x/p (1/16 steps) over the 17 primes ≡ 1 (mod 840) below 3·10⁴: bucket (1/4, 5/16) is present for 100%, the next buckets for 65%, 59% and 35%, and buckets above 3/8 never occur. The sample is too small for a ≥ 90% class-signature claim beyond the first bucket.
Mean U(p)/log³p over p ≡ 839 (mod 840) is 0.696 against 0.192 for other p ≡ 3 (mod 4), already recorded in data/z52b/final_checks.json (keys mean_U/log3_p839mod840 and mean_U/log3_other_3mod4).
Lag-840 residual correlation at primes is 0.637 (3425 pairs) and lag-5880 is 0.582, both already in data/z52b/final_checks.json; the decomposition by p mod 11, 13 was not run.
The 0.70 vs 0.19 excess for p ≡ −1 (mod 840) is already in data/z52b/final_checks.json (recomputed: 0.696 vs 0.192). Attribution of the excess to specific classical identities was not run.
Exact isosceles (x = y or y = z) and near-isosceles (z − y ≤ 4) solutions: zero among all solutions of the 95 primes ≡ 1 (4) below 1200. No degenerate-locus family appears in this range.

Residues of solutions mod p (p < 500, 44 primes): 53.9% of all denominators prime to p are QNR (1300 cases), and 60.4% of the first denominators (781 cases). A modest QNR bias for the smallest denominator, not a lemma.

Resultants between two small exact identity families need the families first: a polynomial ansatz search (x, y, z ∈ Z[k] of low degree with 4/(4k+1) = 1/x+1/y+1/z) plus resultant computations; >1 h coding. Not run.
next: Solve the ansatz for n = 4k+1 with deg x, y, z ≤ 2 over small rationals, then compute pairwise resultants in k.

summary: A smooth-weight version of the divisor-in-AP sum (weights w(C/X)) is the same first-moment object as the S(X)/E(X) measurement in Z1492: witness counts grow at about one third of the uniform prediction from C = 100 to 1000. The Voronoi dual was not written out.

The coupling gcd(4Cp+1, 4C'p+1) | 4(C'−C) (and so the D − C form of the shifted collision) is already stated in BRAINSTORM/z52b_free_fable.md (line 75) and in BRAINSTORM/z52b_translate.md item 228; the collision count for C=1, D=2 is then trivial (common divisors divide 4 or 1).

Divisor collisions between 4Cp+1 and 4Dp+1 are controlled by the gcd coupling gcd | 4(D−C) stated in BRAINSTORM/z52b_free_fable.md line 75 and z52b_translate.md item 228; the restriction on D−C is therefore the known divisor list of 4(D−C).

Digit-lifting substitution p' = bp + r, x' = bx + a (and y, z) into the cleared equation: modulo b, the lifted equation reduces to the original equation at (a, c, d; r), so the first correction constraint is ordinary Hensel lifting with no new content.

Cluster-expansion step: the second cumulant of witness indicators across levels is the covariance measured in Z2559 (mean −0.001) and in Z2796 (mean |corr| 0.032 vs 0.023 shuffled). Higher cumulants were not computed.
Restatement: the tensor rank of the fixed cubic 4xyz − p(xy+yz+zx) is a property of the equation for all p, not of ES solution data, so there is no testable ES content (rule 3).

Optimal transport between witness-divisor residues and all-divisor residues mod 8: witnesses are always ≡ 3 or 7 mod 8 (a ≡ −1 mod 4), so the transport distance (0.57, 1.02, 1.95 for p = 409, 2521, 10009) only restates that constraint.
A CEGIS loop over affine numerator/denominator templates restricted to one residue class needs a template language, a SAT/SMT counterexample step and a verifier; >1 h coding. Not run.
next: Implement the CEGIS loop for templates x = a n + b, y = c n + d, z = e n + f on n ≡ 1 mod 24.

summary: Discrete-log / QNR structure of solution denominators: all denominators prime to p are QNR for 53.9% of cases and the first denominators for 60.4% (n = 781, p < 500). This is the QNR bias of Z0976, not a multiplicity law.
Low-count outliers versus matched controls were done in the H00 lane (BRAINSTORM/z52b_pass1_H00.md, Z0199 class-of-one residuals), which is the same comparison.

PCA (SVD) on the Legendre design matrix (q/p), q < 80, for 1611 primes ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 3·10⁴: variance shares 5.4, 5.3, 5.2, 5.1, 5.1% (no dominant latent factor); the top PCs correlate ≤ 0.10 with the log U residual.
Meta/organisational: a one-page convention table for sources (documentation task, rule 3).
Meta/organisational: a schema for parametric proof objects (rule 3).

Linearisation at solutions: the gradient of the cleared equation is nonzero at all 781 integer solutions for p < 500 (Z0097), so the tangent test is non-degenerate at each solution; no quadratic-correction test was run.

KAM-type persistence, precise version: for consecutive primes p < q ≤ 1000, does a q-solution's first denominator, scaled by p/q, lie within 1 of a p-solution's first denominator? 72.1% of 2076 tests hit, but a scale-matched random partner from the q-solutions hits 73.8%, so there is no persistence beyond the common clustering near p/4.
Recurrence test p → p + 24k needs the full solution sets of primes up to ~10⁵ (about 10⁴ enumerations at up to 10⁵ x-values each) and a pattern match over k ≤ 10³: >30 min compute. Not run.
next: Enumerate solutions for primes ≤ 10⁵ and test whether the residue patterns (x, y, z mod 24) recur along p + 24k.

summary: Covering-system framing of identity classes is in the repo (35 memos mention covering systems, e.g. BRAINSTORM/bsE_sierpinski_moving_integer.md); the delta(M) statistic was not computed.

Mutual information between [U(p)/log³p ≥ median] and p mod M (1611 primes ≡ 1 (4), p ≤ 3·10⁴): 0.0 bits (M=4), 0.19 (8), 0.30 (24), 0.36 (120), 0.44 (840); the permutation baseline at 840 is 0.05 bits (small-sample bias). So ≈0.39 bits of excess information sits in the mod-840 classes, i.e. the known Mordell hard classes (fingerprint lane).
Lenstra 1984 divisors-in-classes is item Z1373 in ES_CONNECTIONS_TODO.md section 1 (pass 1 covered) and B2_ACROSS_FIELDS.md row 8.
Restatement: the Type I condition written as a quadratic-residue condition (p² ≡ −4c²d mod f) is a rewriting of n | x already in the T1 memos, with no new prediction to test (rule 3).

Hand elimination (checked): the Type I substitution x = p·s turns 4xyz = p(xy+yz+zx) into p = yz(4s−1)/(s(y+z)), a rational parametrisation with no further elimination needed. This is the standard Type I parametrisation (Elsholtz–Tao, cf. B2_ACROSS_FIELDS.md), so the Gröbner step returns nothing new.
LP/ILP over a library of campaign identities requires a machine-readable identity library (not in the repo) plus an LP solver setup; >1 h coding. Not run.
next: Build the identity library for p = 1009 in linear form and solve the LP dual for a lower bound on the solution count.

The C-form classes as an explicit covering system with Hough's covering framework are in the repo (BRAINSTORM covering memos, Z1524 family); the density numerics were not run.
Odd squares being uncovered by the (C, a) classes is the T1 statement (FRONTIER.md T1); the characterization of the uncovered set is the U(n) sporadic list (FRONTIER.md §1).

Naive closure P(W_2C | W_C) / P(W_2C) ≈ 2.4 was a pooling artefact: per level, P(W_2C | W_C) averages 0.085 against 0.102 unconditionally and 0.142 for the control P(W_2C | W_{C+1}). No closure under C → 2C beyond chance.

Parity of U(p) over 1611 primes p ≡ 1 (4), p ≤ 3·10⁴: 791 even, 820 odd; split by p mod 8 it is 395/401 (1 mod 8) and 396/419 (5 mod 8). No parity pattern, so no mod-2 involution signal from the count (scripts/z52b_p1_U00_batch2.py).

Witness counts S(X) = Σ_{C≤X} #{a | 4Cp+1: a ≡ −1 (4C)} against the uniform-divisor expectation E(X) = Σ(τ(4Cp+1) − 2)/φ(4C) over 30 primes near 10⁶: median S/E falls from 0.72 at X = 100 to 0.59 at X = 1000; total growth 100→1000 is 134 observed vs 408 expected, and 6 of 30 primes gain nothing (e.g. 1000081 flat at 12). The heuristic overcounts the C-tail, so the witness growth is slower than the uniform model predicts.
next: Test whether the slowdown is a QNR effect (a ≡ −1 mod 4C divisors are forced QNR mod p) or a size effect: compare S/E in C-ranges and against a QNR-restricted model on 10³ primes near 10⁶ to 10⁴.

summary: First winning level C_min(p) within classes p mod 840 (96 classes with ≥ 5 primes): mean modal purity 0.81 against 0.72 over all primes. Little class-determinacy beyond the baseline.

Mean U/log³n over n = m² + 24k (k = 1..5, m ≤ 174, n ≡ 1 mod 4): 1.64, 0.94, 1.01, 1.76, 1.32 (about 85 samples each) against 1.80 over all n ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 3·10⁴. Differences are within sampling noise at this size.
The six U(n) sporadics and their Legendre profiles are in FRONTIER.md §1 (U(n) sporadic list).

The fact that C-form divisors are quadratic non-residues is in BRAINSTORM/y4_t1_numerators.md (Prop 1, Jacobi-symbol sign) and BRAINSTORM/gon_fermat_certificates.md (Lemma CT); the 409/577/5569/9601 exceptions are in FRONTIER.md §2.1.

Checked 1966 C-form divisors (p < 3000, C ≤ 300): all have (a/p) = −1 (scripts/z52b_p1_U00_batch2.py). Jacobi argument: (a/p) = (p/a) = (−C/a) = −1 for a ≡ −1 (mod 4C). Already recorded as BRAINSTORM/y4_t1_numerators.md Prop 1.
Meta/organisational: asks for a REFORMULATIONS.md dictionary, a documentation task (rule 3). The forms are already listed in FRONTIER.md §1.
The squares-plus-sporadic shape is the FRONTIER.md U(n) statement; the stabilisation check for S_I, S_II to 10⁷ was not run.

Random sample of 4000 n ≡ 1 (4), n ≤ 10⁶, C-form levels C ≤ 20: single densities 0.66, 0.44, 0.34, 0.27, 0.22 for C = 1..5; the empirical union has density 0.98, while the Bonferroni lower bound (singles minus pairs over 190 pairs) is −2.06. At 20 levels the bound is useless, so the first-moment route needs far more levels.
The C-form exceptions 409, 577, 5569, 9601 are in FRONTIER.md §2.1 with their search bounds; the C ≤ 10⁶ extension was not rerun (estimate: about 20 minutes in pari).

Three primes near 10⁶, X = 100, 300, 1000: observed/expected witness counts 0.70, 0.68, 0.66 (p = 1000033), 0.92, 0.91, 0.78 (1000037) and 0.53, 0.41, 0.33 (1000081). No extra log factor appears for the first two, but the third is flat; this is the same signal as Z1492 and is recorded there.

Meta/organisational: tagging convention for the merger (rule 3).

summary: win(p, C) for C ≤ 20000 at 5 primes ≈ 10⁴: 8–12 witness levels per prime, so the sequence is sparse. Lag-840 autocorrelation is |ac| < 2·10⁻⁴ for all five, and the lag-1 values (0.1–0.27) are artefacts of a handful of adjacent pairs. No period-840 structure.
Identifying a transformation law for G_p(x) = Σ_C c_C x^C needs a candidate modular or Lambert form, which the item does not supply, plus a fit over several p; >1 h coding. Not run.
next: Fit G_p against candidate Lambert-series transformations x ↦ e^{−2πt} with t ↦ 1/(pt) for p ≈ 10³–10⁴.

summary: p = 409: zero witness divisors for C ≤ 60000 against an expectation Σ(τ(4Cp+1) − 2)/φ(4C) = 37.3 (26.3 at C ≤ 6000). 409 is an R-zero (no (★) word), and FRONTIER.md §2.1 lists it as the first C-form exception, so the first-moment deficit is the known exception.

For 29 primes p ≡ 1 (4), p < 300: every prime factor q ∉ {2, 3, p} of H_{−4p}(0) = ±norm(j(τ_{−4p}) − j(τ_{−3})) is inert in both Q(√−4p) and Q(√−3) (185/185; Gross–Zagier-type inertness). None of the 123 factors q ≡ 3 (mod 4) is a C-form witness for its own p, so there is no link to the divisor classes.
Restatement: 3/(1/x+1/y+1/z) = 3p/4 is ES rewritten as a harmonic-mean identity; no new content (rule 3).
Restatement: the projective-dual formulation of ES is a reformulation with no computable prediction (the item itself notes only upper bounds) (rule 3).
Meta/organisational: GPU port of an existing census kernel is engineering, not a mathematical first step (rule 3).
Same multiplicative-energy test as Z1570 for the divisor set of 4Cp+1 (witness-restricted); values 0.27–0.42 for the non-exceptional primes, empty set for 409 and 577. Nothing beyond Z1570.
The I3 count as a sum over t of divisor counts of tp+1 with d ≡ −1 (mod t) is the definition in I3_DEEP_FABLE.md and FRONTIER.md; the large-t regime map was not recomputed.
Restatement: R_p(m) = qm − p piecewise rewriting of the divisor condition; the van der Corput step has no defined target beyond the existing census (rule 3).
Meta/organisational: teaching / REU problem sheet (rule 3).

Witness mass by C-range: for p = 1000033, 14 of 26 witnesses (C ≤ 1000) come from C ≤ 10, 4 from 11–100, 8 from 101–1000; p = 409 has none. The mass is concentrated at small moduli, so the d-contributions are dominated by small d.
4Cp+1 = ((d+d')/2)² − ((d−d')/2)² is the isosceles parametrisation of a divisor pair; the isosceles lane is in BRAINSTORM/z52b_fingerprint.md and the T1 memos. Nothing new here.
Record primes 73, 1129, 1201, 21169 (A400619): U(p)/log³p = 0.089, 0.055, 0.031, 0.037, all below the 1-mod-4 mean 0.106. The record primes are uniformly U-poor, but four points give little.

The two-term case 3/p = 1/y + 1/z is solvable iff p ≡ 2 (mod 3) (divisors of p² ≡ −p mod 3); the item text in ES_CONNECTIONS_TODO.md (Z0351) already records the p ≡ 2 mod 3 triviality. Not connected to counts.
Renormalisation of R(p) across nested classes p ≡ 1 mod 840·11·13… up to 10⁸ needs witness data for primes up to 10⁸ in each nested class; estimated >30 min compute plus coding. Not run.
next: Compute R/M for primes ≤ 10⁸ in the nested classes 840, 840·11, 840·11·13 and compare means.

summary: σ₂-level sets: M = xy + yz + zx satisfies 4xyz = pM, so p | xyz. Among 2078 solutions for primes ≡ 1 (4) < 1000, p divides M in 32.9% of cases; no 1-parameter family was extracted.

Gauss's theorem (8n+3 is a sum of three odd squares for every n ≥ 0) is classical; checked directly: r₃-type representation exists for every n ≤ 3000. Its ES reading is the ternary-form lane already in the repo; no new single-affine-transform statement emerged.
Markov/Vieta involutions on the ES slices are in MARKOFF_ES.md (§2) and BRAINSTORM/z31_markoff_chen.md.
Divisor-interval and AP bounds for d | 4Cp+1 are the divisor-class analysis in EXSET_SHIFT_DIVISORS.md.
Polynomial identity families as covering maps mod small primes are the T1 and identity-family memos (T1_TEMPLATE.md, MODEL_SPECIFIC.md, GROWING_IDENTITIES.md).
Multiplication-table divisor distribution and the Elsholtz–Tao bounds are in AMPLIFY_EXCEPTION.md and the ET memos (BRAINSTORM/apollonian_reciprocity.md).
Encoding ES identity conditions as residue-class covers is the covering-system framing already in the repo (BRAINSTORM covering memos).

Literature: the thin-sequence prime results (Friedlander–Iwaniec for X² + Y⁴; Heath-Brown type results) give guaranteed primes in thin polynomial families. No ES-valid parameter sequence of that type is identified in the item, so there is no family to apply them to.

Literature: as for Z2316, prime-counting results for recurrence and polynomial thin families. The ES parameter sequences that occur (n ↦ (n+3)/4, 4^s+105, 3·2^s+1) are not shown to fall under those theorems, so nothing was extracted.
The Mordell–Schinzel obstruction is the polynomial-identity statement the Cassels–Pfister route would have to beat (FRONTIER.md §1; T1 memos); no new hypothesis identified.

Least prime witness q | 4Cp+1 with q ≡ −1 (mod 4C), C ≤ 60, over 1125 primes ≡ 1 (4) < 2·10⁴: 1097 have one, with median q = 3 and q < p/10 for 97%. The witnesses are dominated by q = 3 (p ≡ 2 mod 3, the trivial a = 3), so the prime-witness distribution carries no information beyond that.

Literature: Friedlander–Iwaniec (Ann. Math. 148, 1998; arXiv:math/9811185) prove the asymptotic for primes a² + b⁴. The statistic proposed (fraction of Type I divisors that are perfect squares) has no link to this sieve, so nothing to test.

Literature: Merikoski (arXiv:1908.08816) shows the largest prime factor of n² + 1 exceeds n^{1.279} infinitely often. This is a one-variable quadratic bound and does not constrain the divisor classes ≡ −1 mod 4C that define Type I certificates for p² + 4c²d.

Witness divisor sets D_p (C ≤ 40, |D_p| ≤ 8 for the first twelve primes > 100) give quotient sets Q = {a/b} with doubling |Q·Q|/|Q| ≈ 1.7–15 (median 8.7). No approximate-group behaviour at this size, and no random control was run, so the structure is uninformative.

Literature: Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger (Ann. Math. 194, 2021; arXiv:2001.10276) give a uniform bound for rational points on curves of genus ≥ 2 in Mordell–Lang families. The item's curve (two ES solutions sharing x and a ratio) was not written down, so its genus and applicability could not be checked.

Consecutive witness levels (C, C+1) over 1125 primes: mean covariance −0.001, joint/product ratio ≈ 0.6 averaged over C with the small-C pairs dominating; the dependence is weak. The Dickman-type joint law of the consecutive slices was not measured beyond this covariance.
One-parameter identity families over Q(t) are the T1 / Mordell–Schinzel statement (FRONTIER.md T1; T1_TEMPLATE.md).
The Type I norm-form reformulation as a ray-class condition in Q(√−d) is the Type I memo lineage (T1/Type I memos in BRAINSTORM); not rerun.

Smallest meaningful test is a segmented I3 word sieve to n = 10⁹ with per-t event tables (t ≤ 20). The minwords census takes 31 s at 1.2·10⁷ with three uint32 arrays; at 10⁹ this is about 40 min of CPU and ~12 GB of arrays, beyond the 4 GB memory limit unless segmented (>1 h coding). Not run.
next: Write a segmented I3 sieve (blocks of 10⁷) and tabulate P(event_t(n)) and the cross-t correlation to 10⁹.

summary: A Maynard–Tao weighted count needs an admissible k-tuple of slice offsets, a weight function, and a sum over windows of p, i.e. a new analytic-sieve implementation (>1 h coding) plus several hours of runs over primes up to 10⁷. Not run.
next: Choose an admissible tuple of slice offsets, implement MT weights, and compute the weighted proportion of windows with ≥ 2 successful slices.

summary: Murmuration-style test on the I3 minima: R² of log(Tmin_I3) on n mod 840 within n ≡ 1 (4) windows of 2·10⁶ up to 1.2·10⁷ is 0.016–0.038 (about the in-sample floor for 96 class means), so residue classes explain almost none of the variation. No murmuration-type pattern.
bsA_toric_ksb_wahl.md (O174) already records that QNR certificates are never T-singularities, i.e. the Wahl/KSB route to 1/m²(1, ma−1) gives no certificates, and the sign plays no role there.
Bhargava cube / composition for Type II certificates is in B2_ACROSS_FIELDS.md and the Bhargava memos (31 files mention Bhargava).
Kudla/Diff-parity certificate counting is KUDLA_ES.md.
I3 = tuv − u − v as an additive thin basis is the word-form framing in FRONTIER.md §1 and I3_DEEP_FABLE.md; the Erdős–Tetali survey step was not run.

Cross-level dependence of the witness indicators W_C(p), C = 1..30, over 1125 primes: mean |off-diagonal correlation| 0.032 against 0.023 for row-shuffled controls, max 0.215. The excess is small and carried by the shared small-C structure, so no Kubilius-type dependence is evident.
Literature: searched for value-set results for xyz + ax + by + cz; not verified in this pass. The word surface is already analysed in LORENZINI_W.md; no new fibre statement was extracted.
Literature: Chen's theorem (Chen 1973, Sci. Sinica) concerns p + 2 = P₂; the 'switching' analogy is not formulated for ES, so no bijection or near-miss statement was tested.

Literature: Corvaja–Zannier (J. Number Theory 2003, 'On the greatest prime factor of (ab+1)(ac+1)') give Subspace-Theorem bounds on prime factors of products of linear forms. They control size of the largest prime factor, not the residue classes ≡ −1 mod 4C that ES needs.
Literature: Khare–Wintenberger prove Serre's modularity conjecture (Galois representations). No ES counterpart of the 'killing ramification' step is stated, so there is nothing to test.
Certificates for N_e = (p+e)/4 across e are the e-slice lane (EXSET_SHIFT_DIVISORS.md).

Literature: Graham (J. Austral. Math. Soc. 3, 1963, 'A theorem on partitions') proves that every integer > 77 has the partition property in question. The item asks for an affine transfer n ↦ an + b that carries ES solutions to solutions on a residue class, and none was identified or tested.

Literature: Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, Ch. IX, is the standard reference for Galois-cohomological embedding problems. The item's trace of (★) certificates up the tower has no computable first step beyond the census already in the repo, so nothing was extracted.

Computed U(p) and U(p³) from f4_all_30000 for p ≡ 1 (4), p³ ≤ 30000: p = 5, 13, 17, 29 gives U(p) = 2, 4, 4, 7 and U(p³) = 57, 212, 258, 298. Four points are too few to test a linear recurrence in k, and no even-k vanishing was tested here.

The product-covering encoding of (★) in Aff(F_q) has to be designed first (which affine maps, which sets); after that the q ≤ 101 covering check is small, but the encoding design is >1 h work. Not run.
next: Fix the encoding (u, C) ↦ affine map on F_q, then test whether the three-set product covers Aff(F_q) for q ≤ 101.

summary: Legendre-formula bookkeeping over Π_C(4Cp+1) needs a precise statistic for 'which primes can make up the product'; once fixed it is a factorisation count, but the choice of statistic is a design step of >1 h. Not run.
next: Define the prime-multiplicity statistic over C ≤ K and count per prime q by residue class.

summary: The class-equation obstruction Φ_n(q) to 'no certificate' has no concrete form in the item; deriving the counting identity over complete residue systems is a >1 h derivation. Not run.
next: Write the count of certificate-free C mod q as a class-equation sum and test divisibility numerically for q ≤ 101.

summary: Classifying transfer maps (N, e) ↦ (aN + b, ce + d) preserving −1 ∈ Rat_e(N) needs a precise definition of Rat_e(N) (not in the repo) and a search over (a, b, c, d); >1 h design and coding. Not run.
next: Define Rat_e(N) from EXSET_SHIFT_DIVISORS.md and search small (a,b,c,d) for preservation on N ≤ 10⁶.

summary: Odd squares have no certificates at all (T1; FRONTIER.md T1), and the factorisation at n = m² is the same obstruction.
The Brjuno-type success-set characterisation needs a precise index definition and closed-form candidates; the item does not give either, so the design alone exceeds the time box (>1 h). Not run.
next: Fix a Brjuno-type sum over the (★) subroute and fit failure sets ≤ 10¹⁰ against candidate closed forms.

summary: The Brjuno-type difficulty index is not defined in the item; choosing and validating it, then computing it up to 10⁹, is >1 h. Not run.
next: Define the index as a convergent sum over (★) subroutes and correlate with R(p) and Cmin for p ≤ 10⁹.

summary: Θ_p(K) is not defined in the item; a precise definition (prime mass of certificate-capable primes below K) and the comparison bounds from Π_C need design work (>1 h). Not run.
next: Define Θ_p(K) = #{primes q ≤ K: q certificate-capable for p} and compare with the elementary bounds from Π_C(4Cp+1).

summary: Literature: Kang–Kelly–Kühn–Methuku–Osthus (arXiv:2101.04698) is an absorbing method for Ramsey-type problems. No map from Mordell identity families to ES windows is given, so the absorber claim has no concrete test.
Constructing an identity in Z[X]/(X^r − 1, p) that detects ES needs an algebraic search over generating polynomials and a relation-finding step; >1 h coding. Not run.
next: Build P_p(X) = Π_{C ≤ K}(1 − X^{[level C fails]}) for small p and run a linear-relation search over Z[X]/(X^r − 1).

summary: Along the proved family n = 3·2^s + 1 (s = 1..21, Cmin from the minwords census) the sequence is 0,2,0,0,2,2,1,2,1,1,1,4,3,2,1,2,2,1,1,2,1. Least-squares recurrence fits of order 1–4 leave rms residuals 0.95–1.17, so no low-order linear recurrence is visible in 21 terms.
Lifting the F2[T] covering identity coefficientwise to Z[T] is the signed char-2 analysis in FUNCTIONFIELD_ES.md (Thm 6.1 and §6); not rerun.

Literature: Keating–Rodgers–Roditty-Gershon–Rudnick (divisor function in arithmetic progressions over F_q[t]; Lalín and Nguyen follow-ups) give variance asymptotics for divisor sums in APs as q → ∞. This supports a random-model prediction for witness counts, but no ES quantity was computed to test it.
The cone with constant term 1 and its finite-place positivity are in BRAINSTORM/other_rings.md and the function-field cone memos.

ES over F_3[E∖O] for a small elliptic curve needs the coordinate ring, its principal primes, and a sign normalisation at O, i.e. an arithmetic library for Dedekind non-UFD rings; >1 h coding. Not run.
next: Implement F_3[E∖O] arithmetic for one curve and enumerate principal primes of degree ≤ 4 with the e-slice search.

summary: The Mason–Stothers degree bound for FF ES denominators is in SIZE_CONJECTURE.md.
Reduction from composite P to prime divisors in function-field ES is FUNCTIONFIELD_ES.md §1.
The FF e-slice criterion (Lemma 1.3) and its almost-prime reformulation are in BRAINSTORM/ff_erdos_straus.md.
Quasi-polynomial (periodic-coefficient) identities as finite coverings are the B1 statement in B1_LINE.md.
T1 at squares kills polynomial identities in T (FRONTIER.md T1); positivity on an interval adds no new mechanism.

Checking whether ES over F_3[T] with distinct monic denominators fails for deg P ≤ 8 needs F_3[T] factorisation/divisor arithmetic for all monic P (3⁸ and below) and a two-term solver over F_3[T]; >1 h coding. Not run.
next: Implement a two-term solver over F_3[T] (divisors of b² for b = P·x) and run it over monic P of degree ≤ 8 with distinct monic denominators.

summary: Literature: Akiyama (2004, hal-00023233) notes that the Frougny–Solomyak finiteness property (F) of a base β implies β is Pisot; it concerns β-expansions. It does not give a unit-fraction representation of 4/n over Z_{≥0}[φ], so the proposed ES test has no defined integer denominators.
Commuting matrix denominators reducing to number-field ES is in BRAINSTORM/other_rings.md; H00's Z0069 (matrix k=2 trivially solvable) is a related check.
Z[C_2] as an order in Q × Q and the componentwise product ring case are in BRAINSTORM/other_rings.md (ring-variant lane); no separate ES content.
ES in the product ring Z × Z with componentwise positivity is the diagonal of two copies of ES in Z; it is covered by the ring-variant lane (BRAINSTORM/other_rings.md).

Over F_3, D = T²+1 is irreducible and T + √(T²+1) has norm T² − (T²+1) = −1, so F_3(T)(√(T²+1)) has a unit of norm −1 (PROVED, a = T, b = 1). The brute-force search only returned trivial units with b = 0, so the nontrivial unit is found by hand, not by the script.

For each solution of 4/p (95 primes ≡ 1 (4), p < 1200) 1/p² lies in the Z-span of {1/x², 1/y², 1/z²}. This is automatic: p | xyz because 4xyz = p(xy+yz+zx), so some denominator is divisible by p and its square supplies 1/p². The tangent condition is therefore vacuous.
Gradient of F = 4xyz − n(xy+yz+zx) at all 781 integer solutions for primes p < 500: never identically zero, so the cleared surface is smooth at every integer solution in this range.
The norm-denominator census for p ≡ 1 (4) < 2·10⁴ (40 failures among 1125 primes) is in data/z52b/analogues_constraints_20000.txt (analogues lane; scripts/z52b_analogues_constraints.py).
'z is a common multiple of x and y' fails only at p = 2521 below 2·10⁴ in data/z52b/analogues_constraints_20000.txt; the lcm-parametrisation to 10⁶ was not run.
Pairwise coprime denominators never fail below 4000 in the analogues census (scripts/z52b_analogues_constraints.py); the item's own statement.
Squarefree denominators never fail below 4000 in the analogues census (scripts/z52b_analogues_constraints.py); extension to 10⁶ needs-compute, not run.
Prime-denominator constraint: 93 of 269 primes below 4000 fail (analogues census, scripts/z52b_analogues_constraints.py); the classification of the failures was not redone.
Weighted ES a/x + b/y + c/z = 4/n with weights in {1..4}: a sample of seven weight triples gives a solution for every n = 2..40 (bounded search). No obstruction at these sizes.

Solutions of 4/p with all three denominators semiprime (Ω = 2): exist for only 5 of 80 primes ≡ 1 (4) below 1000 (e.g. 89, 257, 509, 677, 761). The semiprime constraint is very restrictive, and no lottery-model comparison was run.
The distinct-denominator census and the splitting lemma are in the analogues lane (scripts/z52b_analogues_constraints.py).

Searched 4/p = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z with x, y, z all pronic (k(k+1)) or all triangular, for 147 primes p ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 2000: no solutions found for either set (search bounded by denominators ≤ about 9·10⁶). Sparsity heuristic (few pronic triples) explains this; no structure identified.

Since lct = 1/a + 1/b − 1/(ab) + 1/c, the equation lct = 4/n is a signed ES variant. Enumerating a, b, c ∈ [2, 40] gives 19 integers n ≤ 1000 (both residues 1 and 3 mod 4) with 4/n = lct, so the family is very sparse.

Literature: Petronio (2020, Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. / Séminaire Lotharingien) surveys the Hurwitz existence problem for surface branched covers; the classical problem is a permutation-triple problem. The averaged-reciprocal variant is not an instance of it, and no ES content was extracted.
Function-field fixed-P counts and their normalisation are in FUNCTIONFIELD_ES.md; the Katz–Sarnak symmetry-type comparison (q = 3, deg P = 8) was not run.

Prime moduli M ∈ [50, 2000] (72 cases, fixed p ∈ {5, 13, 17}): count of (x,y,z) ∈ [1, √M]³ with 1/x+1/y+1/z ≡ 4/p (mod M). Counts are nonzero in 69 of 72 cases (heuristic √M), and zero only for M = 53 (p = 5, 17) and one more case. Small-box solutions are not forced to be trivial.
Restatement: closed-cone remark (positivity set not multiplicatively closed) with no testable ES content (rule 3).
xyz-square failures (20 of 499 primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 below 8000) are in data/z52b/analogues_constraints4_fails_8000.json; the parametric families for square xyz were not characterised here.
Searching P ∈ N[T] with P(1) = n and an N[T]-identity of low degree needs a definition of the identity class and a polynomial-identity solver; >1 h coding. Not run.
next: Define the N[T]-identity template with degree ≤ 2 and search for n = 5, 13, 17.

The sign function on F_q[T][√D] and the e-slice search are in BRAINSTORM/ff_erdos_straus.md.

The char-2 shadow and signed lifts are FUNCTIONFIELD_ES.md §6 and the Z0002 analysis.
Matrix ES with X = xI + N: the k = 2 matrix case is trivially solvable (H00 Z0069, PROVED explicit A, B); the nilpotent-perturbation test duplicates the dual-number item Z0095, which is vacuous.
Matrix ES with k = 2 is trivially solvable (H00 Z0069, PROVED explicit A, B), so the projective M_2(Z) version is covered.
